entries.evidence: The roll bar (the suspension arm p9 2738) hangs on the axle p8 at its foot and holds the roll bar's top axle p32 3707 at its head; two slanted axles 6, p64 and p67, brace that top axle from the frame, each through a toggle joint at its foot (p66, p69) and one at its head (p62, p68, on p32). The file draws each slanted axle 1 LDU off the axis of its head toggle's axle hole (it reaches 14 LDU into it), so the bracing is read as not there: the roll bar swings back on p8 as the swinging arm pushes the shock absorber up against its top axle, and both move, where the function lists them to stay (function 2). Turned half a degree about its foot toggle's hole, each slanted axle runs through both its toggles' holes, as a real axle must, and the roll bar is braced. The shock absorber's top stays on the roll bar's top axle, as drawn; held so, the arm swings and the shock absorber gives through its travel. Booklet: step 12 adds the two slanted axles, step 13's inset shows the shock absorber behind the seat (scans 004, https://lego.brickinstructions.com/en/lego_instructions/set/8832).
